rows.reasoning: For real roots, an odd-index root of a negative number has exactly one real value, an even-index root of a positive number has exactly two real values, and an even-index root of a negative number has none. Thus only the statement that -8 has one real cube root is true.

In quadrant III, sin(theta) and cos(theta) are both negative. Since cos(pi/2+theta)=-sin(theta), the condition gives cos(theta)-sin(theta)=1/3. Squaring and using sin^2(theta)+cos^2(theta)=1 gives 1/9=1-2sin(theta)cos(theta), so sin(theta)cos(theta)=4/9. The requested product is sqrt(sin(theta)cos(theta))=2/3.
